name: RIGETTI COMPUTING

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The strongest counter to refusing is that 'no_model' is being used to avoid an uncomfortable but obvious conclusion. The price-to-tangible-book row is not nonsense — it uses a real balance sheet, the cohort has 158 names, and at 9.4x tangible book against a cohort median of 5.2x it says Rigetti is expensive on the one multiple that actually has a meaningful denominator. Refusing to say so is the failure LESSONS.md warns about from the other direction: the analyst declining to call something expensive because the tooling is imperfect.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Revenue. The fourth-quarter order that Motley Fool reports is worth more than everything Rigetti sold last year is the first real test; a 2027 in which revenue reaches even $50 million would make the price-to-sales frame meaningful for the first time. Until revenue exists at scale, no multiple built on it is a measurement.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Yes, and I am recording it rather than smuggling it through inputs I have just called unusable: at roughly 650x enterprise value to sales and 2,234x enterprise value to gross profit, with negative EBITDA and a $5.1 billion valuation on a tangible book of roughly $540 million that is mostly cash raised from investors, Rigetti may well be very expensive. What I will not do is put a number on it, because the three multiples rows disagree by a factor of twelve ($1.37 on sales against $17.35 at the 75th percentile on tangible book) and the cohort is explicitly unranked. The government issuance is also an observable price: the Department of Commerce took its stake at $12.92, roughly 15% below the market.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Everything that would make this modellable. I did not obtain a qubit roadmap with dates, the terms or size of the fourth-quarter order, the cash burn rate against the $540 million of tangible book, or the milestone schedule attached to the CHIPS award that determines how much of the $100 million is actually disbursed. The interest-coverage flag also says debt is likely understated and I did not chase it.

what_changed: The 8-K filed 2026-09-08 under Items 1.01, 3.02, 7.01 and 8.01, read in full. On 4 September 2026 Rigetti's subsidiary entered an Other Transaction Agreement with the Department of Commerce for a CHIPS Act award of UP TO $100 MILLION. As inducement, on 8 September the company entered a Securities Issuance Agreement to issue the Department 7,739,938 shares at an implied issuance price of $12.92 — roughly 2.3% of the shares outstanding, struck about 15% below the $15.16 market price. The Department covenants not to vote the shares except on changes to authorised shares or par value and on any business combination; there are resale shelf and piggyback registration rights; and if the Department terminates the agreement, Rigetti may repurchase the undisbursed portion of the shares for $1.00 in aggregate. Also in the window: an 8-K on 2026-08-20 under Item 5.02 (officer or director change), Q2 results on 2026-08-06, and a Motley Fool report that the chief executive sold 120,000 shares for $1.9 million after the government agreement was signed. Sector-wide, quantum names sold off on 9 September as Fed rate-hike odds climbed — a duration effect on a zero-cash-flow asset, not a company event.
consensus_case: Rigetti is a $5.1 billion market capitalisation on roughly $8 million of trailing revenue and negative EBITDA, and the buyers know that. What they are paying for is optionality on superconducting quantum computing reaching commercial scale, and in the week before this screen they got two pieces of evidence for it: the U.S. Department of Commerce awarded Rigetti up to $100 million under the CHIPS Act to accelerate superconducting quantum research, and BofA Securities called quantum the 'next fire moment'. The federal government is now a shareholder — it took 7,739,938 shares as inducement for the award. IonQ raised full-year guidance to $450-460 million at its investor day and signed a $1.8 billion deal, which is the revenue scale the sector is arguing Rigetti eventually reaches. A holder is buying a call option on a technology with a national-security sponsor and a government balance sheet behind it, not a cash flow stream, and $377 million of daily dollar volume says the marginal buyer is trading that option rather than discounting anything.
base_case_rationale: I will not supply one. The engine could not compute a normalized FCFF base at all (zero usable years), and the multiples table fails every refusal test in LESSONS.md at once. Manufacturing a growth rate here would be inventing a valuation for a name the model has correctly declined to price.
key_risks: Refusing to model this is NOT a judgment that it is cheap — at 650x sales with negative EBITDA it may be extremely expensive and I decline to put a number on either direction
2.3% dilution from the government share issuance is after the extract's share date and is not in the model's share count

CHIPS award disbursement milestones and any Department clawback
Cash burn against tangible book, and the next equity raise
Any Rigetti guidance for 2027 revenue — the first number that would make a sales multiple mean anything
